clue.text: Most knowing old comedian on street

parts.note: Ernie Wise, of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A veteran comic standing out on the street is the shrewdest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was half of Morecambe and Wise, a much-loved British comedy duo of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: Wise means knowing or sagacious, so the superlative form gives most knowing.

clue.text: One trying to persuade cyclist to go round end of road

indicators.note: to go round means the first piece encloses the next

parts.note: a wheeler is one who rides on wheels, a cyclist

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Coaxing a bike rider to make a loop at the end of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes D from road; 'to go round' puts WHEELER around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax with flattery, so a wheedler is a persuader.

clue.text: Batting stroke after cricket pitch mown

parts.note: the square is the closely mown central area of a cricket ground where pitches are laid
grass that is mown has been cut

explanation.surface: A cricket shot played once the wicket has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the square is the central strip area; 'after' just orders the clue, SQUARE comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A square cut is a cricket shot hitting the ball square on the off side.

clue.text: Concession the Queen holds is a fallacy

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to appease

indicators.note: holds means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: HM, Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A royal allowance that turns out to be a mistaken belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophism is a clever but false argument, a fallacy meant to deceive.

clue.text: Coasting in confused way with no clear view

indicators.note: letters arranged in a confused way are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone drifting along aimlessly, unsure where they are heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in confused way' rearranges COASTING.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known, so takes no firm view either way.

clue.text: Downright rusty, regenerated as thriving business

indicators.note: regenerated letters are remade into a new order

explanation.surface: A thoroughly decayed sector revived into a booming one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regenerated' rearranges DOWNRIGHT RUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A growth industry is a sector expanding fast, a thriving line of business.

clue.text: Deploy a canoe round island here?

definitions.text: Deploy a canoe round island here?

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
to deploy is to arrange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere you might launch a small boat around an isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deploy' rearranges A CANOE to OCEAN plus A, and 'round' puts it around I; the whole clue then describes the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the Pacific region of scattered islands, where canoes have long been the transport.

clue.text: Sailor's first to injure bones in foot

parts.note: a tar is a sailor; with the possessive it gives an extra S

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The first sailor to hurt his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the group of bones in the ankle and rear foot.

clue.text: Company includes one assassinating Caesar's rival

indicators.note: includes means the first piece holds the second

parts.note: to ice is slang for to kill, so an icer is a killer

explanation.surface: A group of conspirators who murder an emperor's opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at Brutus and the assassins, but CICERO was a political opponent of Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero the Roman orator opposed Julius Caesar politically.

clue.text: Rescue from drowning someone ill at ease

definitions.meaning: literally, to fish someone out of water is to haul them from it
an idiom for a person uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings

explanation.surface: Pulling a person in trouble out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a lifeguard might pull someone out of water; figuratively a misfit is a fish out of water.

clue.text: Supply joke over the internet?

parts.note: E is the prefix for anything electronic or online, as in e-mail
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: A request to send a gag by email.
explanation.walkthrough: An e-quip would be a joke sent online; E goes first as in e-mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or provide them with what is needed.

clue.text: One certain knack to lose kilos in form of muscle exercise

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
some, as in 'some people', means certain

indicators.note: to lose means a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a trick is a knack for doing something
K is the abbreviation for kilos

explanation.surface: Advice on a gym technique that sheds weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' drops K from TRICK, leaving TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometric exercise works muscles by tensing them against resistance without movement.

clue.text: Rather like diesel? One may give it a whirl

definitions.text: One may give it a whirl

parts.note: DERV is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles
the suffix -ish means somewhat or rather like

explanation.surface: Asking whether something resembles diesel fuel, then a remark about trying it out.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV (diesel-engined road vehicle) is British usage for diesel fuel. 'Give it a whirl' looks like 'try it', but a dervish literally spins.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling dervish is a Sufi ascetic who spins round in a religious dance.

clue.text: Mediterranean port with more taste

definitions.meaning: a Moroccan city on the Strait of Gibraltar
comparative of tangy, sharper in flavour

explanation.surface: A seaside town said to be more flavoursome.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan port near the Mediterranean entrance, and tangier means having a sharper flavour.

clue.text: Banned from church, suffering Mecca odium next

indicators.note: words that are suffering are knocked about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone ostracised by their faith after hatred from Mecca follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' rearranges MECCA ODIUM NEXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Excommunication is formal exclusion from the sacraments and community of the church.

clue.text: Adorable grenadine cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A lovely mixed drink made with pomegranate syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges GRENADINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endearing inspires affection, so it is lovable or adorable.

clue.text: Practise on carriage whose passenger is late

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a hearse carries the dead, the late

explanation.surface: Running through things aboard a coach with a tardy traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' looks like delayed but means dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise something before performing it.

clue.text: Archers' location guarding crossing after leaders of Saxons take battle in 1066

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters
guarding means the first piece surrounds and protects the second

parts.note: Ambridge is the fictional village in the BBC radio soap The Archers
a ford is a shallow river crossing

explanation.surface: Bowmen positioned by a river crossing as the Saxons go into a famous fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap set in Ambridge. 'after' puts ST first. Archers looks like bowmen at Hastings, but this battle was where Harold beat the Norwegians.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold II defeated Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge in September 1066, weeks before Hastings.

clue.text: Instrument that's struck girl in song about doctor

indicators.note: about means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: Maria is the girl in the song from West Side Story
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A girl from a song hit by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The marimba is a percussion instrument with wooden bars struck by mallets.

clue.text: Standard metal in rake

indicators.note: in means the metal goes inside the other word

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a dissolute man
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A normal metal part found in a garden tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rake' looks like the garden tool; it is a libertine, ROUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine as an adjective means standard or regular.

clue.text: North American tree produces inflammable material

parts.note: a palm is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree from America that yields something that burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is a jellied incendiary used in firebombs.

clue.text: Flyers at work somehow warier going round 3rd class

indicators.note: going round means the jumbled letters enclose the other piece
somehow says the letters are put together in some new way

parts.note: C is the third grade after A and B

explanation.surface: Wary staff surrounding a lowly passenger section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges WARIER, and 'going round' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircrew is the team who fly and operate an aircraft on duty.

clue.text: Reporter's first with a parliamentarian's scams

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament; the possessive gives MP'S

explanation.surface: A journalist and a politician are exposed in frauds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramps is British slang for swindles or rackets.

clue.text: Banger's second taking long time touring America

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A runner-up spending ages travelling the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger's' is 'Banger is': banger is British slang for a sausage. 'Banger' suggests a car or firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Banger is a British slang word for a sausage, from its tendency to burst when frying.

clue.text: Two masters come in to change old school

indicators.note: come in means the pieces enter the following word

parts.note: to alter is to change
MA, Master of Arts, taken twice
MA, Master of Arts, taken twice

explanation.surface: A pair of headmasters arriving to reform an old school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' links; 'come in' puts MAMA inside ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is Latin for nourishing mother, used of the school or university one attended.

clue.text: More wintry with greater risk not starting

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: dicier means riskier, with greater risk

explanation.surface: Colder weather making things more hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops D from DICIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier means colder and more frozen, as in wintry conditions.

clue.text: Terrible scream as it produces many victims

indicators.note: terrible letters are mangled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An awful shriek as something claims numerous casualties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges SCREAM AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is an indiscriminate slaughter killing many people.

clue.text: Sporting competition gets the French fit

parts.note: le is French for the
an ague is a fit of shivering or fever

explanation.surface: A French side gets in shape for a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a competition in which teams play one another for points.
